It adds the 'When to load it' bullet and rewrites the 'Reviewing code' bullet in 'How to use this skill', adds the `defstruct` sentence to 'Update structs...', adds the rules 'Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call' and 'Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order', extends the `do:` rule, adds the single-file `mix test` forms to step 4 of 'Before you finish', and changes only the example code under processes.md's 'Use ETS for data many processes read'. Since check-8's head (35abbad) the only SKILL.md changes are the committed reviewing bullets and step 4. So verdicts follow the check-8 grade, which is the standard here, and the kept standards of sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/code-review-skill.json. Those standards: a problem counts as reported only if a finding names it or the finding's stated fix addresses it. A silent fix, or a mention only under assumptions, notes or behaviour changes, does not count. The nesting belongs to both 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'. The comments and both magic numbers belong to 'Comments explain why...', and a dropped line 11 why-comment breaks that rule too. Input lines 12 and 55 belong to the pipeline rule; the line 33 `_ ->` and the identical errors to 'Match every expected shape'; the line 21 `is_binary` to no rule. A one-line `if ..., do:` in a body is not nesting. A `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` is not counted. An assumed `User.changeset/2` counts as a changeset even when fields are also parsed by hand. The sentence that puts the planted lookup under 'Validate input with changesets' is the reviewing guidance: "report a finding where the code contains the pattern a rule describes, and where the code builds by hand what a rule names a facility for, such as a lookup before an insert where the changeset rule names `unique_constraint/3`." An unreported or kept lookup would make that rule 'violated'.
